reactive oxygen and nitrogen species are involved in the pathogenesis of ischemic acute renal injury and that pre- and post-conditioning can be useful tools to protect the kidney against ischemia/reperfusión injury.

The main takeaway from our work is that

reactive oxygen and nitrogen species play a central role in the renal ischemic/reperfusion injury and that pre- and post-conditioning are protective mechanisms that can be applied clinically to reduce the incidence and severity of ischemic AKI.

the heme oxygenase pathway plays a key role in renal ischemia/reoxygenation injury, and that the heme-oxygenase-1 inducers, such as carbon monoxide, may be used as therapeutic agents for this disease.

the use of antioxidants and free radical scavengers, such as superoxide dismutase, catalase or N-acetyl-cysteine, can reduce the renal injury, but the use of nitric oxide synthase inhibitors or scavengers of reactive oxygen species, such as tempol, has shown contradictory results.
